title: A Wolf for the Hollow
premise: Noor Thornbury, a runaway apprentice with a smuggler's map of the Thornfell mountains etched in memory, wants only to stay forgotten. But when the old gods stir and begin answering prayers in the hollow villages, Noor's rare gift for hearing the land's true voice makes them the only person who can tell a god from an impostor. The impostor is wearing the crown: King Aldric has been unbound from himself, his body a vessel for a hungry thing that feeds on devotion. Guided by Wren, a disgraced royal cartographer who once loved the king, Noor must cross thirteen moons of gathering winter to reach the capital and sever the binding before the thirteenth full moon completes it permanently. In the end, Noor chooses to spend their own memories as the price of unbinding—losing every road they ever memorized but keeping Wren—and the freed king, mortal and diminished, returns the old gods to their proper silence.
about_author: Ulyana Dunmore is the pen name of a former folklorist who spent a decade collecting mountain legends across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes in a converted shepherd's hut and claims she has never once taken the same path home twice.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Fleeing her mentor Maghda's cottage after refusing a dangerous rite, Noor navigates a smuggler's pass at night, establishing her gift: she can feel which paths want to be walked. Emotional beat: wary freedom shadowed by guilt over what she left behind.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Hollow
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the village of Hollowmere, Noor witnesses a grandmother's prayer answered impossibly—a dead orchard blooms overnight. The villagers' joy unsettles Noor, who hears something wrong beneath the blessing. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Maghda Never Taught
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Noor's POV. Reveals why Noor fled: Maghda demanded she bind her hearing-gift shut forever to keep them both invisible. Beat: understanding that flight was also a kind of cowardice.

chapters.title: A Cartographer Without a Map
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Introduces Wren, exiled from the capital for falsifying border maps, drinking in Hollowmere's inn and recognizing Noor's gift when she flinches at the church bell. Beat: two people who recognize each other's hiding.

chapters.title: The Thing That Answers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor prays deliberately, testing the new god, and something answers in her mentor's stolen voice. She realizes the answering presence is not divine but parasitic. Beat: terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren explains court rumor: King Aldric stopped sleeping on the twelfth moon of last year; his edicts grow stranger. The thirteenth turn approaches at midwinter. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Burns Its Saints
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The impostor god demands sacrifice; a neighbor Noor loves is chosen as a 'vessel.' Noor intervenes with a smuggler's trick, exposing herself publicly. Beat: the cost of staying invisible comes due.

chapters.title: Runaways Together
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Noor and Wren flee into the Thornfells together, negotiating trust while hunted by the king's Devoted. Beat: reluctant partnership becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: The Shepherd's Grave
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They shelter at a shrine where an old god still sleeps honestly beneath a cairn. It gives Noor a fragment of truth: the impostor was once a god too, before men bound it into service. Beat: moral complication—the enemy was made, not born.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits she loved Aldric before his crowning, and that her falsified maps were meant to protect him from an assassination route—one that led him to the binding site anyway. Beat: guilt mirroring Noor's own.

chapters.title: The Devoted Ride Out
chapters.summary: Villager Tam's POV (a boy Noor saved). Shows the kingdom through believers' eyes: the crowned god genuinely heals, feeds, protects. Beat: sympathy for the enemy's followers.

chapters.title: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Ambushed at a river ford, Noor uses terrain-sense to drown their pursuers' advance—but one soldier dies looking at her with recognition, not hatred. Beat: first blood, first real grief.

chapters.title: Maghda's Door
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor returns home seeking help; Maghda is dying, her sight burned out by years of shielding Noor. Reconciliation without absolution. Beat: forgiveness asked too late, given anyway.

chapters.title: The Rite Refused
chapters.summary: Maghda's POV, final days. Maghda finally teaches Noor the unbinding rite she once refused to perform, warning its price: the caster pays in memory. Beat: inheritance of burden.

chapters.title: Winter Court
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Disguised as pilgrims, they enter the capital. A court audience reveals King Aldric—magnificent, hollow-eyed, reciting love letters he wrote years ago as scripture. Beat: horror dressed in gold.

chapters.title: The King Who Used to Be
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV, brief and fragmented. Inside the binding, the real king surfaces for moments, leaving messages in his own decrees. Beat: heartbreak—he is still fighting.

chapters.title: Letters in the Margins
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren deciphers Aldric's coded marginalia: instructions to reach the binding stone beneath the cathedral, and a plea—do not save me if it costs another. Beat: love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Hollow Beneath the City
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Smuggler routes lead them under the capital through catacombs no royal map knows. Noor's outlaw knowledge becomes salvation. Beat: the runaway's shame transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Reliquary Gate
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, now a Devoted novice, recognizes Noor and must choose between faith and debt. He lets them pass but reports the breach. Beat: loyalty split down the middle.

chapters.title: Halfway Moon
chapters.summary: Noor and Wren's alternating POV. Trapped by a cave-in, they speak plainly about what they mean to each other, knowing the rite may erase Noor's memories of these weeks. Beat: tenderness under a deadline.

chapters.title: The Impostor Speaks
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The bound god finds Noor in dreams, offering a bargain: serve me willingly and I will spare the king and give you back your roads. Beat: temptation with a truthful face.

chapters.title: What the Old Gods Want
chapters.summary: Shepherd-shrine god's POV, dreamlike. The old gods do not want worship restored—they want to die properly, released from half-life. Beat: reframing the entire conflict.

chapters.title: The Devoted Close In
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The cathedral quarter is sealed; Tam's report has consequences. Wren burns her identity papers, choosing Noor over her old life entirely. Beat: commitment made irreversible.

chapters.title: Blood on the Threshing Floor
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A Devoted raid kills allies among the underground faithful. Noor's grief hardens into something cold; Wren pulls her back from cruelty. Beat: the hero almost loses herself.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. On the twelfth full moon, the binding tightens; the king's self shrinks to a single held note. He spends his last clear hour writing goodbye. Beat: elegy before the climax.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Gathering salt, iron, Maghda's rite, and Wren's maps, Noor writes down everything she cannot bear to forget and gives the pages to Wren. Beat: quiet devastation disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: The Cathedral Ascent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Infiltration during the solstice vigil; Tam covers their approach at last, paying his debt with his freedom. Beat: borrowed courage.

chapters.title: The Binding Stone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Beneath the cathedral, they find the stone—and the truth: the binding was made by the first kings, and the god has been wearing whoever sat the throne for centuries. Beat: the crime is older than anyone alive.

chapters.title: Crowned and Hollow
chapters.summary: Aldric/impostor confrontation POV. The king, nearly gone, confronts them at the stone; the impostor speaks through his mouth, offering Wren Aldric whole if she stops Noor. Beat: love weaponized.

chapters.title: Wren Chooses
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren refuses the bargain—not because she loves Aldric less, but because a returned shell would not be him. She holds the impostor's attention while Noor begins the rite. Beat: duty inverted into love.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The rite begins; Noor pays in memories—her mentor's face, then the smuggler roads, then Hollowmere itself dissolving. Beat: sacrifice rendered viscerally, memory by memory.

chapters.title: The God Remembers Its Name
chapters.summary: Impostor's POV. Unbound, the old god remembers being worshipped honestly and chooses, at last, to die—taking the false divinity of the crown with it. Beat: release rather than victory.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Midwinter moon rises complete; the rite holds. Aldric wakes mortal, weeping, holding Wren's hand without knowing why. Beat: survival that feels like grace.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Miracle
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The Devoted scatter or grieve; Tam buries his robes and walks home to Hollowmere. Beat: ordinary people absorbing an extraordinary ending.

chapters.title: The Blank Map
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor wakes unable to find her way out of the capital's streets—every memorized road gone. Panic, then Wren's hand. Beat: the price made real.

chapters.title: Pages Given Back
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads Noor her own handwriting nightly, returning what can be returned. Some things come back; some don't; some are better rebuilt than remembered. Beat: love as restoration work.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Without a Crown-Thing
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The king abdicates much of his sacred authority, telling the truth about centuries of bindings. Beat: institutional reckoning handled with restraint.

chapters.title: Hollowmere, Again
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Returning to Hollowmere, Noor finds the village remembers her even though she barely remembers it. The grandmother she saved presses bread into her hands. Beat: belonging found where invisibility was sought.

chapters.title: New Roads
chapters.summary: Noor and Wren's shared POV. Noor discovers she can still hear the land—new paths, unmapped, wanting to be walked. She and Wren set out together, no destination fixed. Beat: hope as orientation, not arrival.

chapters.title: A Wolf for the Hollow
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. At Maghda's grave, Noor understands the title at last: the hollow places need guardians who walk their edges, wild and loyal. She takes up the work her teacher began—on her own terms. Final beat: the runaway becomes the keeper.
